subject: ventures/business-loan-offer-comparator
professional: a commercial lending officer / small-business CFO who prices term loans and merchant cash advances (APR by the Regulation Z Appendix J actuarial method; California SB 1235 and New York CFDL estimated-APR disclosures for sales-based financing)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the four sample offers with an independent Python script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/091d6275-30d5-5492-8889-4ef9ed0beb80/scratchpad/business-loan-offer-comparator/indep.py: Reg Z Appendix J style equal unit periods, amount financed = proceeds after prepaid fees, solved by Newton rather than the tool's bisection) and compared with `node -e compare(parseOffers(sampleOffers()))`: bank 9.5%/60 with 1%+$500 -> payment 2,100.19, APR 10.1515%, EAR 10.6374%; SBA-style 11%/120 with 3.5%+$2,500 -> 1,377.50, APR 12.5285%; online 22%/24mo weekly with 4% -> 1,190.54/wk, APR 26.4126%, EAR 30.1421%; 1.32 factor 9 months daily with 3% -> 698.41/day, APR 86.4921%, EAR 137.1304%. All match to 4 decimals. Early payoff of the bank loan at month 12 with 2% penalty: balance 83,595.70, payoff 85,267.61, APR 12.9298% both ways. The MCA's 252-business-day convention checked against a calendar XIRR on real 2026 Fed business days (xirr_hol.py): 87.14% nominal daily vs tool 86.49%, within holiday convention. Gaps found by running edge inputs: a term shorter than one payment period silently becomes one full period (1.1 factor, 1 month, annual payments -> APR 10.0%, true ~120%), and flat fees >= amount give 'NaN%'.
evidence.completeness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 34/34 pass. Every page/README feature exercised via compare(): true APR after fees, effective annual rate, cash received, total repaid, cost of money, cost per $1, payment per frequency (1,2,4,12,24,26,52,252 accepted, 7 rejected), payment as % of revenue and cash-flow cover, early payoff for loans (penalty) and factor offers (discount), ranking and warnings, CSV with quoted commas, flags for factor/daily/APR>60/fees>5%. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origin. breakEvenReturn (calc.mjs:134) is exported and tested but not surfaced on the page; it is not claimed, so not counted against completeness.
evidence.verification: 34 tests pass and pin the core identity (no-fee loan APR = stated APR), fee deduction (net 96,000) and the factor APR band. But 4 of 6 seeded core mutants survived via quality_mutate.py: monthly outflow ignoring payment frequency (calc.mjs:96; this drives the revenue-share and cover columns for weekly/daily offers), factor early-payoff discount sign flipped (calc.mjs:110), cost per $1 on amount instead of cash received (calc.mjs:98), Math.round -> Math.ceil for the payment count (calc.mjs:87). Caught: fees dropped from cash received (calc.mjs:89) and the APR>60 flag threshold (calc.mjs:120). No test pins a fee-bearing APR or factor APR to a hand value (only `> 9.8` and `50 < apr < 60`).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (150 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs. Pure exported functions, guarded bisection IRR, quoted-CSV parser, HTML escaped. Defects: payment count rounds silently (term 10 months quarterly -> 3 payments = 9 months; 1 month annual -> 1 payment at 12 months); flat fee >= amount is accepted and renders 'NaN%' and cost per $1 'Infinity'/-6.27 (calc.mjs:75 checks feeFlat >= 0 only); a payoff month just under the term (59.9 of 60) rounds k to n and shows a zero-balance 'early payoff'; breakEvenReturn is dead on the page; one 300-character object literal per offer (calc.mjs:71).
evidence.claims: No-warranty text on index.html:131, README and guide; 'Not modelled' and 'Unverified' lines on index.html:108 are honest. No-upload claim backed: grep finds no fetch/sendBeacon/XMLHttpRequest in calc.mjs, usage.mjs or index.html; usage counts are localStorage only with DNT/GPC honoured (usage.mjs:34). Guide worked example checked: bank lowest APR (10.15%), ten-year loan most dollars (71,300) with lower APR than online (12.53 < 26.41), advance 3.3x the next APR - all true. One false claim: guide line 38 'the same 1.3 over six months is more than double that' - recomputed ratio is 1.88 (monthly), 1.97 (weekly), 1.99 (daily), never above 2. The not-modelled list omits sales-based (percentage-of-receipts) remittance, the defining feature of an MCA.
evidence.fitness: Walked an owner's job: paste four offers, read lowest APR, fewest dollars, monthly outflow vs revenue, early-payoff cost, export CSV. Works in seconds and puts a factor rate and a loan APR in one column correctly, which is the job. A CFO would still need to supply an expected MCA term themselves and convert a lender's monthly or simple-interest quote to an APR before typing it in.
evidence.domain: Against Reg Z Appendix J (actuarial method, unit period = payment interval, APR = period rate x periods per year, prepaid finance charges reduce the amount financed) the method is right: fees come off proceeds, APR is nominal per-period IRR, EAR shown separately. California 10 CCR 940-946 and NY CFDL estimated-APR disclosures for sales-based financing also use Appendix J with an estimated term; the tool's 'expected months' input plays that role, and its 252-business-day year lands within 0.7 points of a daily-unit calendar solve. Departures: MCA remittance is modelled as a fixed daily payment (no holdback percentage or sales-based term estimate), and the factor early-payoff discount is applied to the whole remaining payback rather than to the unearned finance charge, which is how many MCA prepayment discounts are written. Both are stated-limits gaps, not errors in the arithmetic.

defects.what: A term shorter than one payment interval is silently rounded up to one full interval (and non-multiples are rounded to the nearest payment), so the APR is solved over the wrong time span: 1.1 factor, 1 month, annual payments reports 10.0% APR instead of about 120%; 10 months quarterly becomes 9 months. Should reject or warn when termMonths*ppy/12 is not a whole number.

4 of 6 seeded core mutants survive: monthly outflow ignoring frequency (feeds the revenue-share and cover columns for weekly/daily offers), factor early-payoff discount sign, cost per $1 denominator, payment-count rounding. The affordability test uses a monthly offer only and the early-factor test uses a 0 discount; no fee-bearing or factor APR is pinned to a hand value.
Flat fees equal to or above the amount pass validation and render 'NaN%' APR and an Infinity or negative cost per $1 instead of an input error.

Guide says a 1.3 factor over six months has 'more than double' the twelve-month APR; recomputed ratio is 1.88 (monthly), 1.97 (weekly), 1.99 (daily), never above 2 (the test itself only asserts 1.8x).
A payoff month just under the term (59.9 of 60) rounds the payments-made count to the full term, so the early-payoff table shows a zero-balance payoff as if early.

MCA remittance is modelled as a fixed payment over a typed term; holdback (percentage of receipts) and the estimated-term method CA/NY disclosures use are not modelled and not listed under 'Not modelled'; the factor prepayment discount is applied to the whole remaining payback rather than the unearned finance charge.
breakEvenReturn is exported and tested but never used on the page (dead feature code).

verdict: The arithmetic a lending officer cares about is right. Against an independent Reg Z Appendix J style solve, all four sample offers match to four decimals (bank 10.1515%, SBA-style 12.5285%, weekly online 26.4126%, 1.32 factor daily 86.4921%), the early-payoff APR matches (12.9298%), and the 252-business-day MCA convention lands within 0.7 points of a calendar solve on real 2026 business days. Fees correctly reduce the amount financed. Disclaimer, not-modelled and unverified lines are present and the no-upload claim holds. Weak spots: a term shorter than one payment interval is silently stretched (1.1 factor over one month with annual payments shows 10% instead of ~120%), fees >= amount print 'NaN%', the guide's 'more than double' is false (1.88-1.99x), and MCA holdback is neither modelled nor listed as a limit. The 34 tests pass but 4 of 6 seeded core mutants survive, including the monthly outflow for weekly and daily offers. Does not meet the bar: verification 2 (correctness 3, claims 3, median 3). Finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: reject non-whole payment counts and proceeds <= 0, fix the guide sentence, and add tests that pin a fee-bearing APR, a weekly monthlyPay and a non-zero factor discount.
